text:
maya: Kicking off network activation probes for au-syd cluster. I pushed the transit attachments and updated RTs, running sanity checks now.
liam: Thanks — can you call out which route tables you changed?
maya: Modified tgw-rt-prod-01 to add 10.240.0.0/16 -> attachment-ausyd, and added a low-priority 0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-gw-ephemeral for smoke tests.
liam: Do we have the peer account accepted on the TGW side? Last time the cross-account attach stayed Pending for a while.
maya: infra-bot: tgw-attach status for attachment-ausyd: PendingAcceptance.
infra-bot: Please run `aws ec2 accept-transit-gateway-vpc-attachment --transit-gateway-attachment-id tgw-attach-0a1b2c3d` from the infra account.
ryan: I accepted it a minute ago, status changed to Available.
maya: Running quick traceroute from a provisioner pod to an external IP to validate NAT egress: `traceroute -n 8.8.8.8` -> hits 10.240.0.1 then 54.77.x.x then 8.8.8.8. Latency 45-60ms.
sre-oncall: For production we should avoid ephemeral NAT for sustained GPU provisioning traffic — cost and port limits. Any plan to attach an EIP pool or NAT Gateway autoscaler?
liam: We plan to attach nat-gw-provisioning (HA pair) in the next step, but need to confirm route priority so it doesn't affect control-plane traffic to the central region.
maya: Noted. For now tests use ephemeral so we can scope the TGW routing changes. I'll add a canary route with higher metric for provisioning prefixes only: 10.241.0.0/16 -> nat-gw-provisioning.
devops: Heads up: ENI limit in the AZ could restrict max GPU instances. If we push full fleet, we risk hitting 50 ENI limit on the bootstrap instance type. Recommend increasing ENI quota request ticket now.
ryan: Opened quota ticket with cloud provider, ref CLD-4921. ETA 24-48h. We should gate full scale until that's approved.
liam: Also watch for cross-AZ data transfer; our routing via TGW could force heavy egress back to central region. Estimate additional $0.02/GB if we don't localize caching.
sre-oncall: Running DNS delegation check: did we add the private hosted zone delegation for ausyd into account DNS?
maya: I created zone redwood-int.au-syd and added NS records to the parent zone in Route53 with the four delegated nameservers. Command used: ```aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZPARENT --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"redwood-int.au-syd.","Type":"NS","TTL":300,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"ns-1.awsdns-xx.com."},{"Value":"ns-2.awsdns-xx.net."},{"Value":"ns-3.awsdns-xx.org."},{"Value":"ns-4.awsdns-xx.co.uk."}]}}]}'```
liam: Can you run an authoritative lookup from a central region resolver to confirm delegation?
maya: `dig @ns-1.awsdns-xx.com redwood-int.au-syd NS +short` -> returns the four nameservers. Delegation looks good.
devops: Quick validation checklist I recommend before handoff: 1) TGW attach Available, 2) Route tables show only scoped prefixes for provisioning, 3) NAT pair in place for scale, 4) ENI quota ticket in progress/approved, 5) Private DNS delegation verified, 6) BGP (if used) shows advertised prefixes.
ryan: I ran `aws ec2 describe-transit-gateway-route-tables --transit-gateway-route-table-ids tgw-rtb-0abcd` and confirmed the provisioning CIDR entries exist with correct association.
sre-oncall: Small probe: can an instance in au-syd reach the metrics endpoint in central-prod without going over public internet? 
maya: `curl -v http://metrics.central.internal/health` -> 200 OK, TTL shows path via TGW, not public.
liam: OK, once quota ticket is green we'll swap ephemeral NAT for the HA pair and escalate route metrics. After that we can trigger GPU bootstrap jobs at 10% capacity to validate autoscaler and ENI behavior.
sre-oncall: I'll schedule a 30-min smoke window at 0400 UTC and be on standby. Add post-checks for route flaps and kernel drops on the ENI.
maya: Adding runbook snippet to the cluster ops doc and attaching smoke checklist. Will post link when done. :thumbsup:
